plan.topic: Unapproved 'retatrutide' peptides and emergency visits: NSW Health data on emergency-department presentations linked to unapproved peptides (July 2025 to September 2026)
plan.angle: Lead with NSW Health's 19 Oct 2026 release: 1,180 emergency-department presentations linked to unapproved peptide use from 1 July 2025 to 30 September 2026, with monthly presentations rising from 5 to 217. Use the retatrutide share only if the NSW Health epidemiology PDF states it, worded as presentations 'mentioning' retatrutide, and credit it to that document. Drop the 18% admission figure unless the PDF states it. Quote NSW Health's line that these products may contain unknown or harmful substances or the wrong ingredients, and say these are linked presentations, not lab-confirmed contents. Status credited to Lilly with a full date: retatrutide is investigational and not approved anywhere as of Oct 2026, and the real drug exists only in Lilly's trials. Better route: ask a prescriber about approved options or a clinical trial. No sellers or vials, a calm tone, 'Not personal advice' plus the full prescriber line, 170 words or fewer.

plan.why: Gray-market 'what's confirmed?' Shorts that name retatrutide are our strongest lane (median 103.5 for gray-market Shorts; 120 for retatrutide-named Shorts). The NSW Health data is a new dated fact we haven't published, and the title template differs from 10-22's CBS Short. | fact-check: The primary source exists: NSW Health media release of 19 Oct 2026 (https://www.health.nsw.gov.au/news/Pages/20261019_00.aspx). It confirms 1,180 emergency-department presentations associated with peptide use from 1 July 2025 to 30 September 2026, and monthly presentations rising from 5 in July 2025 to 217 in September 2026. The release names retatrutide only as one of several claimed peptides (BPC-157, GHK-Cu, TB-500, retatrutide, CJC-1295). It doesn't give the 71%, the 833 or the 18% admitted. The 71% appears in press coverage (The Daily Aus, Pharmacy Daily) as visits 'mentioning' or 'naming' retatrutide, and may come from the NSW epidemiology PDF (https://www.health.nsw.gov.au/epidemiology/Publications/unapproved-peptide-use.pdf), which I couldn't extract. The radar's wording 'involving products sold as retatrutide' is stronger than the source: a mention is not confirmed exposure. 18% admitted is unverified, so drop it unless the PDF states it. Use the release's own contents caveat: products 'may contain unknown or harmful substances, be incorrectly labelled or contain different strengths or ingredients than advertised'. The lead format is approved.

NSW Health (Australia) reported on 19 October 2026 that 1,180 emergency department visits from July 2025 to September 2026 were associated with peptide use, with monthly visits rising from 5 to more than 217. Retatrutide is one of several peptides named, alongside BPC-157.
Retatrutide is investigational and not FDA-approved (Lilly Medical, reviewed 26 August 2026). Genuine supply is through clinical trials, or limited expanded access that a doctor requests. Ask a prescriber about approved options or a trial. Used one and feel unwell? Get medical help.

factcheck.summary:
I checked both sources directly, and every claim in the script matches them.

**NSW Health media release, 19 October 2026:**
- It reports 1,180 emergency department presentations "associated with peptide use" between 1 July 2025 and 30 September 2026.
- Monthly presentations rose "from just five in July 2025 to more than 217 presentations in September 2026", so "more than 217" is exactly right.
- It names retatrutide, BPC-157, GHK-Cu, TB-500 and CJC-1295.
- The s5 quote matches the release word for word.
- The Poisons Information Centre number, 13 11 26, is correct.

**Lilly Medical page, last reviewed 26 August 2026:**
- It calls retatrutide investigational and "not currently approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA)".
- It says expanded access requests "are initiated by the treating physician".
- The eligibility rules are narrow (BMI of 35 or more with refractory obesity and serious complications), so "limited" is a fair word.

**Framing and safety:** The "here's the catch" re-hook correctly says the count covers peptide use in general, not confirmed retatrutide. There's no dosing, sourcing or buying information. The prescriber line, the "Not personal advice" line and the advice for anyone already unwell are all there, and "follow for more" is correct because no related long-form has been published.

I found only two minor wording points, with fixes below.

issues.claim: ...one thousand one hundred and eighty emergency visits associated with peptide use since July twenty twenty-five.
issues.problem: The narration gives only the start date, so it sounds like the count runs up to today. The source window ends on 30 September 2026, and the stat label already says so. Our rules ask for the timeframe to be spoken, not only shown on screen.
issues.fix: On October nineteenth, twenty twenty-six, N-S-W Health reported one thousand one hundred and eighty emergency department visits associated with peptide use from July twenty twenty-five to September twenty twenty-six.

issues.claim: Used one and feel unwell? Get medical help.
issues.problem: This is accurate, but the release gives a more specific step: call the NSW Poisons Information Centre on 13 11 26, or Triple Zero (000) if someone is unconscious or having trouble breathing. The 000 line is missing from the on-screen list.
issues.fix: Optional: change the third list item to "In NSW: Poisons Information Centre 13 11 26; emergencies 000 (NSW Health)". Keep the narration as it is to stay within the word limit.

notes: Caption card 1 is built from a phonetic spelling ('TWENTY TWENTY-SIX,') instead of the on-screen numeral, and ends on a trailing comma.
Caption card 2 reads 'ONE THOUSAND ONE' then cuts off mid-number — doesn't match the 1,180 stat pill and ends on a bare number.
Caption card spells the date out as 'TWENTY TWENTY-FIVE' instead of using the numeral form from on-screen text.
Caption 1 ends on an ellipsis ('FROM FIVE... TO MORE'), which is a banned caption ending.
Numbers are spelled as words ('FIVE', 'SEVENTEEN') instead of matching the '5 → 217+' stat pill numerals.
The generic magnifying-glass icon has no label and doesn't connect to 'the count covers' / 'NSW Health names' — the visual doesn't explain what's being searched.
Caption spells 'NSW' out as hyphenated letters ('N-S-W') instead of the literal code.
Caption 'RETATRUTIDE AMONG SEVERAL,' ends on a trailing comma, a banned ending.
Caption spells BPC-157 as 'B-P-C ONE-FIVE-SEVEN' instead of the literal drug code — in a video about unapproved peptides this is a factual/safety-relevant garble.
Caption '"THESE PRODUCTS MAY' ends on the auxiliary verb 'MAY', a banned caption ending.
The box + red question mark is a fairly generic, low-information visual for this beat.
Caption 'LILLY'S MEDICAL PAGE,' ends on a trailing comma.
Caption spells FDA as 'F-D-A' with hyphens instead of using the literal 'FDA' on screen.
Caption 'GENUINE SUPPLY IS THROUGH' ends on the preposition 'THROUGH', a banned ending.
Following caption 'ACCESS THAT A DOCTOR REQUESTS.' reads grammatically awkward/garbled.

audio.soundNotes: Music is already sitting right at the top of the target window (-13.5 dB under voice, -14.3 in pauses), so gain stays at 1.0 — don't push louder. Trimmed three dense SFX clusters (t≈20.5–21.8, t≈27.3–28.6, t≈31.7–33.9, t≈71.5–72.7) down to 3–4 hits by dropping redundant ticks/blips/swooshes, pulled the one badly clipping pop at t21.39 (-8.8 dB) down into the -17 dB speech pocket, and boosted the "Investigational" transition swell/whip at t49 (a pause/reveal moment that was under-target at -14.9 dB) up toward -9 dB so it lands with real weight. Added two bespoke, understated cues — a clinical alert chime on the NSW Health warning and a low tension drone under "may contain unknown substances" — to sell the caution beats without ever competing with the narrator.
